topics.title: Energy Bands and Carrier Statistics
topics.syllabus: Energy bands in intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, equilibrium carrier concentration, direct and indirect band-gap semiconductors.

cards.title: Equilibrium carrier concentrations
cards.bodyHtml: At equilibrium the product of electron and hole densities is fixed by the material and temperature alone — doping shifts the split, never the product.

cards.title: Direct vs indirect gap
cards.bodyHtml: In a direct-gap material the conduction minimum sits directly above the valence maximum, so recombination emits a photon. Indirect materials need a phonon too, which makes them poor light emitters.

topics.title: Carrier Transport
topics.syllabus: Carrier Transport: Diffusion current, drift current, mobility and resistivity, generation and recombination of carriers, Poisson and continuity equations.

cards.title: Drift and diffusion
cards.bodyHtml: Drift is driven by a field, diffusion by a concentration gradient. The two coefficients are linked by the Einstein relation, so knowing mobility gives diffusivity for free.

cards.title: Diffusion length and continuity
cards.bodyHtml: Excess minority carriers injected at one point decay exponentially with distance. The diffusion length is how far they get before recombining.

topics.title: P-N Junction and Diodes
topics.syllabus: P-N junction, Zener diode, LED, photo diode and solar cell.

cards.title: Built-in potential and depletion width
cards.bodyHtml: The depletion region widens under reverse bias and narrows under forward bias. Its width scales as the square root of the total junction voltage.

cards.title: LED and the direct-gap requirement
cards.bodyHtml: An LED is a forward-biased junction in which injected carriers recombine radiatively. That needs a direct band gap, which is why silicon — the material everything else is made of — cannot make one, and GaAs and its alloys can.
cards.pitfallHtml: An LED is forward biased and a photodiode reverse biased — the same structure, opposite quadrants. Reading the bias off the circuit tells you which device the question is really about.
